subject: Clarify: backup purge lag, emergency restore window & subprocessor coverage
messages:
From: Laura Zhang <laura.zhang@clinichealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@procureco.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Backup purge lag & cross-border log question

Hi Neha,

Quick follow-up from our compliance team: we saw a note in the onboarding checklist that backups may be retained for an additional 30–45 days in cold storage before final purge. ClinicHealth needs a firm statement on 1) the maximum backup purge lag, 2) whether any backup copies or logs will be stored or replicated outside the EU (we are regulated), and 3) whether a short-term emergency restore window is available for legal holds.

Can you confirm details (and share the current purge timeline CSV so our legal team can review)? We also have an outstanding DPA amendment request to reflect the retention carveouts — I attached our requested language to the Doc we circulated.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Zhang
Head of Privacy & Compliance
ClinicHealth

Attachments: backup_purge_questions.txt (text)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Laura Zhang <laura.zhang@clinichealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Backup purge lag & cross-border log question

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. Tagging Kim (legal) and Karthik (ops) to confirm technical and contractual bits. Quick answers while they chime in:

- Maximum purge lag: standard is 14 days after client deletion for hot/cold snapshot lifecycle, with an additional grace stage in long-term immutable archive that can extend to 45 days for certain escrow/restore windows.
- Cross-border storage: by default EU-region customers have backups stored in eu-central-1 only; however, some subprocessors (backup replication partners) operate a tri-regional replication pipeline and may have metadata routed via other regions. We will not replicate content to the US for ClinicHealth unless explicitly authorized in the DPA addendum.
- Emergency restore: we offer a documented 30-day emergency restore window for legal holds as an add-on; we can make an exception to extend to 45 days on a case-by-case negotiated amendment.

I attached the current purge timeline CSV and the DPA amendment draft for your comments (see attachments). Kim/Karthik — please confirm the subprocessor list and whether the SFTP archival vendor (ChainStore S3 Mirror) stores encrypted snapshots outside eu-central-1 when replication is enabled.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security & Privacy PM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: backup_purge_timeline.csv, DPA_Amendment_draft.docx

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Laura Zhang <laura.zhang@clinichealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Backup purge lag & cross-border log question

Adding legal context here — thank you, Neha. A couple of notes for the amendment and CLINIC-specific language:

1) DPA clause: we can add a carveout that explicitly states backups are retained for up to 45 days in immutable archive for restore/forensic needs, and that any extension beyond 45 days requires written approval.
2) Cross-border statement: we will include a line that "Redwood will not replicate or transfer content-at-rest outside EU regions for EU-region customers unless Customer-authorized or required by law."
3) Subprocessors: we must enumerate the backup/replication subprocessors and include the country of operations and their SOC attestation level. Karthik, please confirm ChainStore mirror's replication defaults and the region list so we can enumerate in Appendix B.

Laura — once we have the vendor region list, legal will prepare a short DPA amendment and a mutually agreeable signature flow (DocuSign).

Kim Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Laura Zhang <laura.zhang@clinichealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:51:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Backup purge lag & cross-border log question

Folks — quick ops confirmation after vendor check: ChainStore S3 Mirror (our archival SFTP/backups partner) keeps a primary copy in eu-central-1. Replication is optional and configured per-customer; default for EU-region customers is replication disabled. When replication is enabled for disaster recovery, secondary replicas may be staged in eu-west-1 and ap-south-1 (never in us-east-1 unless customer explicitly enables global replication).

Also: immutable archive lifecycle looks like this for ClinicHealth if we adopt the 45-day carveout:
- Day 0: customer issues deletion request or retention trigger
- Day 0-14: hot snapshot retention (fast restore possible)
- Day 15-30: cold snapshot (restore requires ops runbook, 6–12 hours)
- Day 31-45: immutable archive (forensic restore on request, 24–72 hours)
- >45: final purge unless legal hold or written exception granted

For emergency legal holds: we maintain an internal escalation path that pauses purge at any stage; ops needs the signed LOE from customer and ticket in the legal queue. Marissa — can you confirm we have runbook steps documented for the 24–72 hour immutable restore path?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Laura Zhang <laura.zhang@clinichealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Backup purge lag & cross-border log question

On Fri, Jun 20, 2025 at 09:51 AM, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> For emergency legal holds: we maintain an internal escalation path that pauses purge at any stage; ops needs the signed LOE from customer and ticket in the legal queue. Marissa — can you confirm we have runbook steps documented for the 24–72 hour immutable restore path?

Hi all — confirmed. Runbook exists in the internal runbook repo and I've exported the checklist to the shared Drive link below. Key operational notes for ClinicHealth:
- We can place a purge hold within 2 hours of a valid LOE and confirmed ticket.
- Full immutable-archive restore (readable snapshots delivered to secure SFTP) target is 48 hours SLA for standard business hours; weekends may push to 72 hours.
- We will not perform cross-border transfer of snapshot content without explicit DPA amendment language.

Next steps for closure:
1) Kim to draft DPA amendment language enumerating subprocessors + carveout and explicit cross-border prohibition without auth.
2) Neha to share the purge timeline CSV with ClinicHealth legal (done).
3) ClinicHealth to confirm whether they want the optional extended 45-day emergency restore add-on or stick to the standard 30-day offering.

Drive export: https://drive.redwood/ClinicHealth/DPA_Amendment_draft.docx

Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference
